questions.q: In the breach response lifecycle, why does containment come before full assessment?
options: Containment is actually the last step in the lifecycle, not an early one
Regulations require containment to happen exactly 72 hours after detection
Assessment is unnecessary once containment is complete
Waiting until the incident is fully understood would let the exposure continue, so stopping it takes priority even with an imperfect picture
questions.explain: The lifecycle accepts an imperfect early picture in exchange for stopping the ongoing exposure immediately, rather than waiting for full clarity before acting.

questions.q: Which role is primarily responsible for notification obligations and liability during a breach response?
options: Security
Legal
Leadership
Communications
questions.explain: The lesson assigns legal to notification obligations and liability, while security handles technical investigation and containment, communications handles public messaging, and leadership handles broader business-risk decisions.

questions.q: Under GDPR's breach notification framework, when must affected individuals (not just the supervisory authority) be notified?
options: Only if the breach lasted longer than 72 hours
Only when the breach is likely to result in a high risk to those individuals
Only when the supervisory authority is not notified
For every single breach, regardless of risk level
questions.explain: The supervisory authority notification and the individual notification use different, deliberately separate thresholds — individuals are notified only when the breach is likely high-risk to them specifically.

questions.q: Why does the assess step of breach response depend on earlier chapters of this course?
options: Assessment only matters after notification has already occurred
Classification labels and audit logs are what let an organization quickly determine how sensitive the exposed data was and who touched it
Assessment is a purely legal function with no technical dependency
Classification and logging are unrelated to determining breach severity
questions.explain: Without classification labels and audit trails already in place, an organization has to reconstruct how sensitive the data was and who accessed it from scratch during the incident itself.

questions.q: What is the well-known GDPR timeframe this lesson cites for notifying the supervisory authority after becoming aware of a breach?
options: Exactly 24 hours in all cases, with no exceptions
Within 30 days of the breach occurring
Without undue delay, and where feasible, not later than 72 hours
There is no time limit specified under GDPR
questions.explain: GDPR Articles 33-34 set the 'without undue delay, and where feasible, not later than 72 hours' standard for notifying the supervisory authority, unless the breach is unlikely to pose a risk to individuals.
